articles.title: A textural moment: why the fashion world is falling in love with opera coats
articles.summary: From Jennifer Lawrence to Kate Moss, the fuzz-trimmed garments are proving popular with celebrities, while others are DIY-ing their way into the trend. While puffer jackets have dominated winter wardrobes for years, this winter an alternative is emerging: the fuzz-trimmed opera coat.
body: Originally worn over formal evening gowns, new interpretations come in floor-grazing and cropped styles and are being worn with everything from minidresses to jeans.

Jennifer Lawrence wore a Dior opera coat, complete with a furry shawl collar, to the premiere of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping this week, while Kendall Jenner has been photographed in a maxi yellow version, which she wore with slouchy trousers. Having fuzzed their way down various catwalks, Staud, DÔEN, Zara, Next, Free People and Marks & Spencer are all stocking the new “it” coats.
Rixo’s floral embroidered and faux-fur trimmed version, worn by both Lawrence and Kate Moss, has sold out several times.
“I think the appeal of these coats is that they feel both luxurious and wonderfully nostalgic,” says Orlagh McCloskey, the cofounder and creative director of the London-based brand.

articles.title: Vitamin D, fiber and flavor: how healthy are mushrooms?
articles.summary: Experts say there are many reasons to boost our consumption of mushrooms and incorporate them into our diets. Mushrooms aren’t quite as popular in the US as they are in other parts of the world.
body: People in the US also don’t consume as wide a variety of mushrooms as other parts of the world, says Dr Krystle Zuniga, a board-certified oncology dietitian based in Austin, Texas. “I often think of them as a forgotten vegetable,” she says, though she clarifies they are technically fungi.
Yet there’s good reason to boost our consumption of mushrooms and incorporate different varieties into our diets. Here’s what experts say about the health benefits of mushrooms.

“The selling points for mushrooms for many years were that they taste good, and they don’t have any bad stuff in them,” says Dr Robert Beelman, professor emeritus of food science and director of the Center for Plant and Mushroom Foods for Health at Penn State University. “There’s very little fat, no sugar, very few calories.”

Mushrooms’ savoury, umami flavor also makes them a particularly good option for anyone looking to eat less meat. “I often recommend replacing up to 50% of ground meat with chopped mushrooms for meatballs, tacos or meat sauce recipes,” says Marisa Moore, a registered nutritionist based in Atlanta.

articles.title: What 8 Cool Food People Outsource for Thanksgiving
articles.summary: This story was previously published as part of that series. Subscribe to Eater Today to see more of our editors’ boldest opinions about dining culture writ large. A few Novembers ago, I had a mild crash out over puff pastry.
body: If you buy something from a link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

Then I remembered the puff pastry. For some reason, I attached a moral imperative to the idea of making the whole pie from scratch, and spent the next two weeks poring over puff pastry recipes that felt like casual guides to wizard-tier alchemy. I loved to cook, but I simply wasn’t a big baker. (I also didn’t own a food processor, unless you counted my Magic Bullet.) My mother eventually brought me down to Earth. “Just buy it,” she told me over the phone, undoubtedly rolling her eyes. “Everyone knows it’s a pain in the butt.” Even the Barefoot Contessa herself, she reminded me, famously avoids the time-consuming task ( “Nobody wants to make puff pastry!” ).

Those words set me free. Once I realized that I could outsource my puff pastry, and the source of my Thanksgiving stress, I was finally able to relax and enjoy the holiday. Folks take pride in their Turkey Day dishes, as they should, but there’s nothing wrong with accepting a little help.

articles.title: Winter’s Top Boot Color Isn’t Brown or Black—It’s Burgundy
articles.summary: Elegant yet versatile, wine red is the ultimate winter hue for elevating both neutrals and brighter hues. Shop our favorite burgundy boots now.
body: Burgundy is having a moment (as evidenced in our ballet flat and handbag trend reports), but now it’s footwear’s time to shine. On the runways, deep, wine-colored boots walked the Hermès and Lanvin’s fall 2026 shows, and appeared off-duty in fashion week street style looks captured in London, Paris, and Milan.

High or low, scrunched or structured, oxblood-colored boots look great styled a multitude of ways: pair the knee-high version with a long leather coat for a Carmen Sandiego-inspired look, or wear with jeans tucked into the shaft for an equestrian-minded moment.

The shade’s strong presence on the runways and in street style serves as a testament to burgundy’s staying power, just in time for the colder seasons. From deep oxblood tones to bordeaux and brighter cherry reds, it’s a hue that’s essentially a neutral, serving as an alternate stand-in for black, with a subtle pop of color.

From ankle boots to knee-highs, stiletto heeled to flat, and in materials like crocodile to Intrecciato, there’s a version that suits your taste and budget. Below, a few of our favorite burgundy styles to wear for the months ahead.

articles.title: How to Style Wide-Leg Jeans, According to the Street Style Set
articles.summary: Wide-leg jeans are one of the most popular denim trends, and this is how to style yours, with inspiration straight from the street style set.
body: Over the past few years, denim trends have been a particularly hot topic here at Vogue HQ. From the divisive barrel leg and ultra-low-rise styles, to the return of skinny jeans, there has been no shortage of denim shapes to debate–and, in many cases, internet discourses to fuel. For 2026, however, the denim styles leading the conversation feel, by comparison, reassuringly familiar.

Of them all, wide-leg jeans arguably have the most universal appeal. Unlike a straight-leg, which has a more uniform look, this silhouette can be tweaked to create different results. You can go for a baggy skater style, a flared fit that will appeal to aspiring Chloé girls, or even a more tailored pair that resembles formal trousers. This variety also means that the styling opportunities are plentiful. This fall’s street style galleries have been awash with wide-leg jeans, worn in ways that prove there is no one-size-fits-all formula.
points: Wide-leg jeans are one of the most popular denim trends, and this is how to style yours, with inspiration straight from the street style set.

articles.title: Farrar, Straus and Giroux Celebrated Eight Decades of Literary Greats
articles.summary: Few literary presses can claim a Rolodex as studded with boldface names as Farrar, Straus and Giroux. This week, the publishing house, whose authors have been awarded dozens of National Book Awards, Pulitzer Prizes, and Nobel Prizes in Literature, toasted its 80th anniversary with a distinguished…
body: The guest list, which gathered prominent cultural and artistic personages, featured a mix of FSG’s coterie of best-selling writers from over the years. The night united early-career contemporary authors like Madeline Cash ( Lost Lambs) and Raven Leilani ( Luster ) with established literary lions such as Jonathan Franzen, André Aciman, and Jeffrey Eugenides. The decorated crowd also included filmmaker John Waters, Emmy Award winner Rebecca Miller, actor and editor Tavi Gevinson, and booksellers James Daunt and Sarah McNally.

Guests were treated to a soaring performance of Philip Glass’s “Songs from Liquid Days” by Anthony Roth Costanzo (whose debut memoir Countertenor was published last month), fresh off his starring turn in Lincoln in the Bardo at the Met. The revelry continued into the night with sounds from New York City funk and soul band The Ruckus and a late-night surprise DJ set by multiple-Grammy-winning artist Ahmir Thompson, better known as Questlove, who also just so happens to be the publisher of FSG imprint AUWA Books.

articles.title: How to Set Up Alexa Wishlist Alerts for Black Friday and Cyber Monday
articles.summary: Amazon’s Black Friday and Cyber Monday sale has officially started —but keeping track of the best discounts yet to land and figuring out which deals are worthwhile can be a challenge.
body: Then head to the Alexa mobile app and go to More in the top left (the three horizontal lines) > Settings > Notifications > Amazon Shopping and toggle on Deal Recommendations under the Shopping Recommendations options. This ensures you’ll receive notifications for items that appear in your shopping activity.

If Alexa finds an upcoming deal on something in your Saved for Later, your Wish List, or in your Shopping Cart, you’ll receive a pop-up alert on your Echo Show display or see a yellow light ring on your Echo speaker. You can also ask, “Alexa, what are my notifications?” to hear a list of deals it has compiled thus far. You can also say "Alexa, let me know when [product name] goes on sale."

Alexa can detect deals up to 24 hours in advance, so you can either ask it to remind you again when a deal starts or request that it buy the item when the deal goes live. Simply say, “Alexa, buy it for me,” and it’ll charge the default payment and send the item to the default delivery address on your account.
